mazos.descripcion: Verbos modales (can, could, may, might, must, have to, should, would…): significado, completar, elegir, traducir, reescribir y errores típicos.

campos: I advise you to leave now, or you'll miss the bus.
You'd better leave now, or you'll miss the bus.
You ___ pay to enter the museum. It's free!
You don't have to pay to enter the museum. It's free!
You ___ have seen John yesterday. He's in Japan.
You can't have seen John yesterday. He's in Japan.
It was a mistake not to study.
He {{c1::must}} be really rich. Look at his car!
Debe de ser muy rico. ¡Mira su coche!
You ___ see a dentist about that tooth.
You should see a dentist about that tooth.
{{c1::Can}} you help me with my homework?
You {{c1::shouldn't}} go to bed so late.
Tienes que llevar puesto el cinturón.
Se dice wear o put on a seatbelt.
I will can help you next week.
I will be able to help you next week.
No se ponen dos modales juntos.
Más vale que no llegues tarde.
no tener que / no hace falta
You don't have to come if you don't want to.
No tienes que venir si no quieres.
No es prohibición: puedes hacerlo si quieres.
Tengo que llamar a mi madre esta noche.
Para reglas externas (leyes, trabajo) se prefiere have to.
You {{c1::mustn't}} touch that cable. It's dangerous!
He can to play the piano.
I would travel more if I had more money.
Viajaría más si tuviera más dinero.
I'm sure she isn't the teacher.
You ___ wear a tie. It's a casual party.
You don't have to wear a tie. It's a casual party.
You {{c1::needn't}} bring anything. We have plenty of food.
No hace falta que traigas nada. Tenemos comida de sobra.
= You don't have to bring anything.
I'll be able to help you tomorrow.
can no tiene futuro ni infinitivo: will can → will be able to.
I had to wait for two hours.
When I was young, I ___ run ten kilometres without stopping.
When I was young, I could run ten kilometres without stopping.
I might go to the party, but I don't know yet.
A lo mejor voy a la fiesta, pero aún no lo sé.
Suele indicar algo menos de certeza que may.
Es incontable: an advice advices → a piece of advice. El verbo es advise.
I'll be able to see you on Monday.
We {{c1::don't have to}} wear a suit to the office.
No tenemos que llevar traje a la oficina.
You're not allowed to use your phone here.
Don't worry, we have plenty of time.
Mi hermano sabe cocinar muy bien.
You'd better hurry, or you'll miss the train.
Más vale que te des prisa o perderás el tren.
Hurry up! = ¡Date prisa! · in a hurry = con prisa.
We ___ go to the cinema tonight. What do you think?
We could go to the cinema tonight. What do you think?
He must have forget his keys.
I hope I'll ___ come to your wedding.
I hope I'll be able to come to your wedding.
Después de will no puede ir can.
Los modales no usan do en preguntas: se invierte el orden.
I'm sure they forgot about the meeting.
They must have forgotten about the meeting.
Deducción sobre el pasado: must have + participio.
Students {{c1::mustn't}} use their phones during the exam.
Los estudiantes no pueden usar el móvil durante el examen.
It can get very cold here in winter.
Aquí puede hacer mucho frío en invierno.
Habla de lo que es posible en general, no de una predicción concreta.
You look pale. You {{c1::should}} go home and rest.
Tienes mala cara. Deberías irte a casa a descansar.
You ___ have told me! I would have helped you.
You should have told me! I would have helped you.
Reproche: «deberías habérmelo dicho». must have sería una deducción.
We ___ wear a uniform at my school. It's the rule.
We have to wear a uniform at my school. It's the rule.
Es una norma (obligación), no un consejo.
Se le debe de haber olvidado.
No tienes que venir si no quieres.
You don't have to come if you don't want to.
Va al final de la frase.
Decisión tomada en el momento de hablar.
That {{c1::can't}} be Tom. He's in London this week.
Ese no puede ser Tom. Está en Londres esta semana.
No debes fumar en el hospital.
Can you remind me to call Ana?
remember = acordarte tú. remind = hacer que otro se acuerde.
Do you know how to drive?
Te avisé del tiempo que iba a hacer.
Con will va entre will y el verbo.
Arrepentimiento o crítica sobre el pasado
Algo que no hiciste (y estuvo mal no hacerlo).
I'm sure he didn't take it.
Deducción negativa sobre el pasado: can't have + participio.
I {{c1::would}} buy a house if I had enough money.
Me compraría una casa si tuviera suficiente dinero.
Her eyes are red. She {{c1::must have}} been crying.
Tiene los ojos rojos. Debe de haber estado llorando.
I {{c1::can}} play the guitar, but not very well.
Sé tocar la guitarra, pero no muy bien.
Deducción negativa (estoy seguro de que NO)
Es lo contrario de must (deducción). Para esto NO se usa mustn't.
I'm exhausted. I {{c1::should have}} gone to bed earlier.
Estoy agotado. Debería haberme acostado antes.
Deducción sobre el pasado (seguro que SÍ)
Se le debe de haber olvidado.
You ___ park here. It's a fire exit.
You mustn't park here. It's a fire exit.
Would you like me to open the window?
The lights are on. They {{c1::must}} be at home.
Las luces están encendidas. Deben de estar en casa.
Casi solo en preguntas con I o we: Shall I help you?
I could swim when I was five.
Sabía nadar cuando tenía cinco años.
Habilidad general en el pasado. Para un logro concreto se usa was able to: I was able to fix it.
They {{c1::must have}} gone out. The lights are off.
Deben de haber salido. Las luces están apagadas.
It's polite to say please and thank you.
Es de buena educación decir por favor y gracias.
I don't have to get up early tomorrow.
wake up = despertarse. get up = levantarse de la cama.
No hace falta que traigas nada.
También: She / I might not come.
No seas maleducado con tu hermana.
I'm sure he is at home.
Is it OK if I sit here? (formal)
When I was a child, I {{c1::could}} climb trees easily.
Cuando era niño, podía trepar a los árboles fácilmente.
Me gustaría un vaso de agua.
I'd like a glass of water.
You should see a dentist about that tooth.
Deberías ir al dentista por esa muela.
It's a secret. You ___ tell anyone.
It's a secret. You mustn't tell anyone.
Tomorrow is Sunday, so I {{c1::don't have to}} get up early.
Mañana es domingo, así que no tengo que madrugar.
We missed the bus by two minutes.
Perdimos el autobús por dos minutos.
También: I miss you = te echo de menos. Perder un objeto = lose.
No hace falta que me esperes.
You don't have to wait for me.
Irregular: steal – stole – stolen. Robar a una persona o un banco = rob.
It wasn't necessary for us to wait.
He's only six, so he {{c1::can't}} drive.
Solo tiene seis años, así que no puede conducir.
His car is still here. He ___ have taken the bus.
His car is still here. He must have taken the bus.
Deducción sobre el pasado: seguro que sí.
Puede que hayan perdido el autobús.
Más vale que te des prisa.
«Saber + infinitivo» (sé nadar, sé conducir) se dice con can: I can swim.
Dogs are not allowed in the shop.
No se permiten perros en la tienda.
be allowed to + verbo: Am I allowed to park here?
Después del modal, verbo en infinitivo (sin -s).
Consejo (igual que should, algo más formal)
I was able to run fast when I was young.
I could run fast when I was young.
I ___ go out tonight, but I'm not sure yet.
I might go out tonight, but I'm not sure yet.
I'm sorry, I won't {{c1::be able to}} come to your party.
Lo siento, no podré ir a tu fiesta.
ablehelpI'llyoubetotomorrow
I'll be able to help you tomorrow.
Posibilidad en el pasado: might have + participio.
Take an umbrella. It {{c1::might}} rain later.
Llévate un paraguas. Puede que llueva luego.
Estaba escondido detrás de la puerta.
You must to wear a helmet.
I {{c1::could have}} passed the exam if I had studied.
Podría haber aprobado el examen si hubiera estudiado.
I ___ swim when I was three.
I couldn't swim when I was three.
mindtheyouclosingwoulddoor
I'm not sure, but she {{c1::might}} be at the library.
No estoy seguro, pero puede que esté en la biblioteca.
We could go to the beach tomorrow.
Podríamos ir a la playa mañana.
My parents don't allow me to go out at night.
Mis padres no me dejan salir por la noche.
Podía trepar a los árboles fácilmente.
{{c1::Could}} you pass me the salt, please?
Can también vale, pero could es más cortés.
We could go to the cinema.
She {{c1::has to}} work on Saturdays. Her boss says so.
Tiene que trabajar los sábados. Lo dice su jefe.
have to sí se conjuga: she has to.
follow / break the rules = cumplir / saltarse las normas.
We'd {{c1::better}} not be late for the interview.
Más vale que no lleguemos tarde a la entrevista.
It isn't possible that she is 40.
You ___ use a pen. A pencil is fine too.
You don't have to use a pen. A pencil is fine too.
My advice is to take a break.
It's possible that he is ill.
When she was young, she {{c1::couldn't}} swim.
Perhaps they didn't get the message.
They might not have got the message.
Se le debe de haber olvidado.
También: He / They must have forgotten.
En preguntas, el modal va delante del sujeto.
You'd better hurry, or you'll miss the train.
Más vale que te des prisa o perderás el tren.
'd better + verbo sin to. Implica una consecuencia negativa. Negativa: had better not.
She don't have to work today.
have to se conjuga con does / doesn't.
I have to wear a uniform at work.
Tengo que llevar uniforme en el trabajo.
Se conjuga: has to, had to, will have to. El pasado de must es had to.
I hope I'll be able to come to your wedding.
Espero poder ir a tu boda.
___ I help you with your bags?
Shall I help you with your bags?
You {{c1::mustn't}} tell anyone. It's a secret.
No se lo debes contar a nadie. Es un secreto.
I have to wear a uniform at work.
Tengo que llevar uniforme en el trabajo.
She ___ be at work. I've just seen her at the gym.
She can't be at work. I've just seen her at the gym.
I can't find my keys. I ___ have left them at the office.
I can't find my keys. I must have left them at the office.
After three hours, I finally ___ fix my bike.
After three hours, I finally was able to fix my bike.
Para un logro concreto en el pasado se usa was able to (o managed to), no could.
You'd {{c1::better}} leave now, or you'll be late.
Más vale que te vayas ya o llegarás tarde.
En negativas y preguntas se usa yet: Have you finished yet?
Los modales no llevan -s en 3ª persona.
It isn't necessary to bring food.
You {{c1::can't}} park here. It's a private garage.
No puedes aparcar aquí. Es un garaje privado.
can't también expresa prohibición (más informal que mustn't).
He's been yawning all evening. He ___ be tired.
He's been yawning all evening. He must be tired.
You ___ better study for the exam.
You had better study for the exam.
They {{c1::might have}} got lost. Let's call them.
Puede que se hayan perdido. Llamémoslos.
I ___ like a cup of tea, please.
I would like a cup of tea, please.
He {{c1::can't have}} seen me. I was hiding behind the door.
No puede haberme visto. Estaba escondido detrás de la puerta.
Ayer tuve que trabajar hasta tarde.
must no tiene pasado: se usa had to.
I {{c1::will}} call you tomorrow, I promise.
Te llamo mañana, te lo prometo.
She ___ be French. Her accent is perfect.
She must be French. Her accent is perfect.
I don't like tea. Can I have coffee instead?
No me gusta el té. ¿Puedo tomar café en su lugar?
instead of + sustantivo o -ing: instead of going out.
It's a good idea to book a table.
In my country you {{c1::have to}} be 18 to vote.
En mi país hay que tener 18 años para votar.
It was necessary for me to work on Sunday.
apologize for algo: He apologized for being late.
Can I go to the bathroom?
Más formal: May I go to the bathroom?
You didn't have to do that.
Hay que tener 18 años para votar.
No hace falta que te preocupes.
Deducción positiva (estoy casi seguro de que SÍ)
You've been working all day. You must be tired.
Llevas todo el día trabajando. Debes de estar cansado.
Lo contrario es can't: You can't be tired!
I couldn't swim when I was a child.
Se le debe de haber olvidado mi cumpleaños.
